q: Work outside-in on head injury. What is the order?
a: scalp → skull → bleeds around brain → brain → cord
scalp, skull, bleeds around the brain, brain, cord
scalp to skull to bleeds around brain to brain to cord
outside-in: scalp → skull → bleeds → brain → cord
why: Work from the outside in: scalp → skull → bleeds around the brain → the brain itself → the cord.

q: Primary brain injury already happened. What three secondary problems do you fight?
a: low oxygen, low blood pressure, infection
low oxygen / low blood pressure / infection
why: Fight the secondary stuff: low oxygen, low blood pressure, infection.

q: Trauma patient has a slow heart. What two problems are on your short list?
a: pressure in the head or spinal cord injury
head pressure or spinal cord / neurogenic
Cushing’s / head pressure OR spinal cord injury
pressure inside the head, or a spinal cord injury
why: Trauma + slow heart rate = only two things: pressure in the head, or a spinal cord injury.

q: Slow heart + HIGH blood pressure after trauma — what do you think?
why: Slow heart + HIGH blood pressure = pressure inside the head (Cushing’s).

q: Slow heart + LOW blood pressure after trauma — what do you think?
why: Slow heart + LOW blood pressure = spinal cord / neurogenic shock.

q: Name Cushing’s triad.
a: high wide BP, slow heart, irregular breathing
high and wide blood pressure, slow heart, irregular breathing
high wide BP + slow heart + irregular breathing
high wide BP, slow HR, irregular breathing
why: Cushing’s triad: high wide BP, slow heart, irregular breathing.

q: What BP pattern fits Cushing’s better — 200/90 or 160/110?
why: High and WIDE BP: systolic shoots up, diastolic stays nearer normal. Example 200/90. Regular high blood pressure usually climbs together like 160/110.

q: May you give nitro to drop Cushing’s high BP?
why: Do not give nitro to drop that blood pressure. A drop in BP after a brain injury is a secondary killer.

q: Central nervous system equals what?
why: Central nervous system = brain + spinal cord.

q: Meninges outside to inside — name the three layers.
why: Meninges outside to inside: dura, arachnoid, pia.

q: Where is CSF made, and about how much?
why: CSF is made inside the brain (about 125 mL).

q: Late rising pressure shoves the brainstem down which hole?
a: foramen magnum at base of skull
why: Foramen magnum = big hole at base of skull. Late rising pressure shoves brainstem down that hole (herniation).

q: Basilar skull fracture clues — name three.
a: raccoon eyes, Battle’s sign, CSF nose/ear
raccoon eyes, Battle’s (mastoid), CSF from nose or ear
raccoon eyes + Battle’s sign + CSF leak
raccoon eyes, Battle’s sign, CSF from nose or ear
why: Basilar: raccoon eyes. Battle’s sign (mastoid bruise). CSF from nose or ear.

q: Epidural bleed classic pattern?
a: hit, pass out, wake up talking, pass out again
why: Epidural: usually artery, fast. Lucid interval — down → up → down.

q: Subdural bleed — fast or slow, and who is it common in?
a: slow delayed; older people and alcoholics
slow; common in older people and alcoholics
why: Subdural: usually a vein. Slow. Common in older people and alcoholics.

q: Sudden worst headache after a head event — which bleed pattern?
why: Subarachnoid: sudden worst headache. Clutch the head and drop.

q: Concussion CT — normal or bruise? About what percent never pass out?
a: CT normal; about 90% never pass out
CT looks normal; ~90% never pass out
CT looks normal; about 90% never pass out
why: Concussion: CT looks normal. About 90% never pass out.

q: Bones out of place pinch the cord without cutting it. What can happen when pressure comes off?
a: feeling and movement returned when pinch gone
pressure off → feeling and movement can return
why: Bones can pinch without cutting. Same numbness and paralysis until the pinch is gone; pressure off can return feeling and movement.

q: Name board reasons after trauma.
a: unconscious, numb/paralysis, neck/back pain, or you do not believe them
unconscious; numbness or paralysis; neck or back pain; do not trust them
unconscious, numb/paralyzed, neck/back pain, or do not believe them
unconscious / numb or paralyzed / neck or back pain / you do not trust them
why: Board for unconscious, numbness or paralysis, neck or back pain after trauma, or you do not believe them.

q: Full-face helmet blocks airway, or head rattles inside — what do you do?
a: take it off — two people, no neck bend
why: Take it off if full-face blocks airway, head rattles, arrest, or cannot immobilize with it. Two people; do not bend the neck.

q: Trauma airway — which maneuver, and may you use an NPA?
why: Jaw thrust. No NPA.

q: One minute of low oxygen after a brain injury — what happens to death risk?
why: One minute of low oxygen after a brain injury makes death much more likely.
